source: Beger, Yi, Fu, Denton, Moskvichev, Tsai, Rajamanickam, Mitchell (2025) Distinguishing Performance From Competence in Evaluations of Humanlike Abstract Reasoning
finding: Gap 1. On ConceptARC with text grids, o3 beats humans on output accuracy, so the accuracy gap is closed for the best reasoning model. But about 27 percent of its correct outputs rest on unintended or wrong rules, versus about 7 percent for humans.
numbers: ConceptARC 480 tasks, pass@1, temperature 1.0. Text, o3 low 68.3, medium 77.1, low+tools 67.9, medium+tools 75.6. Claude Sonnet 4 medium 60.2, +tools 55.0. Gemini 2.5 Pro medium 66.0, +tools 60.4. Humans 73.0 (Prolific). Unintended or incorrect rules among correct outputs: o3 and Gemini ~27%, Claude ~19%, humans ~7%.
quote: AI reasoning models have exceeded human performance on the ARC-AGI-1 benchmark, but does that mean
limits: Single benchmark; o3 high effort not tested; rule labels hand-coded (4 annotators, 192 rules, kappa 0.70); human rules missing for wrong outputs and 19% of correct ones unclear; repeated-run rule label identical in only 54-56% of cases.
agent_relevance: Accuracy alone overstates relational competence. A scaffold that checks the stated rule against the intended abstraction (objects, not cell values) matters more than a higher score. Supports a rule-check step in O7.

source: Beger et al. (2025) ConceptARC visual modality and effort/tool effects (same paper, section 4 and Appendix I)
finding: Reasoning effort helps in text but not in vision; Python tools help in vision. In the visual modality, models often find the right rule but fail to apply it.
numbers: Visual accuracy medium+tools: o3 29.2, Claude 6.9, Gemini 5.8; without tools o3 5.6-6.7, Claude 5.2, Gemini 4.2. Correct-intended rules vs correct grids: o3 40.0 vs 29.2, Claude 14.4 vs 6.9, Gemini 23.5 vs 5.8 (gaps 10.8, 7.5, 17.7 points; McNemar p<1e-5). Text o3 low to medium effort: 68.3 to 77.1.
limits: Repeated runs on 48 tasks only; grid-size recognition from images is a perception confound.
agent_relevance: Apply vs induce split: a separate execution step (code or explicit grid writer) may recover accuracy even when the rule is already right. Medium effort is about a 16K reasoning budget.

source: Beger et al. (2025) rule vocabulary analysis (Figure 3)
finding: Humans phrase rules with object words; models phrase them with grid-cell words. Evidence of lower-level, less relational encoding even when right.
numbers: Rules analysed: humans 2456, Claude 261, o3 363, Gemini 290 (correct grids only, text). Humans use more objectness terms (object, shape, line) and fewer grid terms (cell, row, value).
limits: Preliminary manual term lists; humans saw images, models saw integer text, so the input format differs.
agent_relevance: Re-encode text grids into objects before reasoning (links to the ACRE text vs symbolic gap, K11).

source: Minegishi, Furuta, Kojima, Iwasawa, Matsuo (2026) Matching Object or Relation? Tracing Abstract Reasoning Inside VLMs
finding: Gaps 3 and 8. Direct RMTS test on 2026 vision-language models using the comparative-psychology paradigm. Capability tier, scale, object count and noise decide whether the model picks the relational or the object match. Chain of thought lifts weak models to near ceiling.
numbers: Relational rate no-CoT: GPT-5.4 100.0, GPT-5.4-mini 32.2, Claude Opus 4.6 100, Claude Haiku 4.5 42.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro 100. CoT: GPT-5.4-mini 83.4 (+51.2), Haiku 99.9 (+57.4). Gemma-4 26.3 (E2B) to 100 (31B); Qwen3.5 50.0 (0.8B) to 89.3 (9B). Numerical-equality relation: GPT-5.4 82.5. Noise sweep: Gemma-4-26B 100 to 92, Gemini 3.1 Flash 99 to 86. 729 canonical trials, both orders, nonce labels.
limits: Metric is a bias rate, not accuracy; geometric stimuli only; images not text; frontier models near ceiling on the easy relations; head ablation on ARC-AGI-1 is only head-level causal evidence.
agent_relevance: The claim of Monk et al. 2024 that language models fail RMTS is out of date for 2026 frontier models. Step-by-step CoT moves weak models from object bias to relational choice at modest cost: a cheap scaffold lever.

source: Minegishi et al. (2026) mechanism section: two competing circuits
finding: Inside open models an early circuit groups by surface object features and a late circuit groups by abstract relation. With CoT the relational answer survives ablation.
numbers: Ablating relational heads: ARC-AGI-1 cell accuracy drops more than random-head ablation for Gemma-4-26B and 31B. Gemma-4-26B head-ablated direct answers fall to chance, with CoT back to 100%. Qwen3.5-0.8B never forms the relational circuit (Rel% 50.0); 4B and 9B reach 77.3 and 89.3.
limits: Small open models; mechanistic claims rest on RSA and mediation; not tested on text-only LLMs.
agent_relevance: CoT rescues the relational answer through a different route than the direct circuit, which supports an explicit write-the-relation step rather than trusting a single forward pass.

source: Camposampiero, Hersche, Wattenhofer, Sebastian, Rahimi (2025) Can Large Reasoning Models do Analogical Reasoning under Perceptual Uncertainty?
finding: Gap 1. Reasoning models do well on clean Raven-style matrices but collapse when the problem gets longer, has wider value ranges and noisy attributes, despite spending more tokens. A neuro-symbolic abductive model stays robust.
numbers: I-RAVEN to I-RAVEN-X: o3-mini 86.6 to 17.0 with 3.4 times more reasoning tokens; DeepSeek R1 80.6 to 23.2; ARLC (neuro-symbolic) 98.6 to 88.0.
limits: Symbolic attribute inputs, not pixels; 2025 models only; only two reasoning models.
agent_relevance: More tokens do not buy relational generalisation. Out-of-range and noisy inputs are the failure mode to test; an explicit rule-induction and execution step beat long CoT here.

source: Stevenson, Pafford, van der Maas, Mitchell (2024/2025) Can large language models generalize analogy solving like children can?
finding: Gap 3. Children and adults transfer letter-string analogy rules from Latin to Greek to a symbol alphabet. Models do not. Part of the cause is missing prerequisites (predecessor, second successor), not only misreading.
numbers: Mean proportion correct Latin/Greek/Symbol: adults .88/.91/.89 (n=62), children .62/.66/.67 (n=41), GPT-4o .85/.63/.48, Claude-3.5 .68/.62/.46, Llama-3.1 405B .79/.74/.27, Gemma-2 27B .60/.39/.14 (n=54 each). Alphabet effect p<.001 for every model, none for humans.
limits: Models are GPT-4o era, not reasoning models; repetition rules transfer fine, ordering rules do not.
agent_relevance: Splits comprehension from abstraction: repeat rules transfer, order-dependent rules need an ordered alphabet that is not flexibly mapped. A scaffold should write the ordered alphabet out explicitly before applying a rule.

source: Lee, Song, Yoon, Park, Kang (2025) The Curious Case of Analogies: Investigating Analogical Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Gap 3. Models encode the relation in mid-upper layers when they succeed; failures come from missing relational information or from failing to apply it to the new entity. Patching hidden states recovers a part.
numbers: Patching the first pair in incorrect cases changes behaviour in up to 38.4% (Gemma-7B); revisions to correct answers up to 38.1%; Llama-2-13B +32.3%, Qwen2.5-14B +35.6%. Probe accuracy on analogical vs non-analogical situations up to 82.9%.
limits: Open 7B-14B models; proportional and story analogies; interventions need internal access.
agent_relevance: Applying a relation is as much a bottleneck as encoding it, so a scaffold should separate extraction (name the relation) from application (instantiate it on the target).

source: Khojasteh, Jiang, De Giorgis, van Harmelen, Ilievski (2026) YARN: LLM-derived abstractions plus structural mapping for narrative analogies
finding: Gap 2. An explicit text pipeline (decompose into units, abstract roles, then map) beats raw LLM answers on far analogies and multiple choice, but not on near analogies.
numbers: MCQ: Qwen YARN 0.46 vs best LLM-only 0.41; Llama 0.45 vs 0.28 LLM-only. Mapping without abstraction 0.17 (Qwen), below 0.25 chance. ARN near: Qwen CoT 0.79 vs YARN 0.69; far: Qwen zero-shot 0.52 vs YARN 0.47, but Llama YARN 0.46 vs 0.42. ARN far stays near or below the 0.50 chance baseline.
limits: Small open models (Qwen, Llama), not frontier; not an equal-token comparison; embedding-based mapping is weak; no reasoning models.
agent_relevance: Closest evidence to a text relational bottleneck: abstraction helps far analogies only, hurts near. No equal-token test against CoT, so gap 2 stays open.

source: Raemaekers, Finn, De Houwer (2025) Assessing the Relational Abilities of LLMs and Large Reasoning Models, Behavioral Sciences 16(1) 45
finding: Gaps 3 and 9 (partly). On a nonword syllogism battery from relational frame theory, reasoning models beat plain LLMs; analogy and same/opposite are weakest; accuracy falls with more premises and irrelevant premises.
numbers: Analogy block: LLaMa 3.3 70B 47.31, LLaMa 3.1 405B 55.19, GPT OSS 20B 83.27, GPT OSS 120B 83.85. Same/opposite: 55.18, 61.25, 91.11, 93.56. Randomised premise order: analogy 48.27, 55.39, 77.50, 79.81; GPT OSS 120B same/different 99.80 to 91.84. 1,364 problems times 10 variants.
limits: Four models; no human data; temperature 0.75; text itself gives an inconsistent 70B analogy figure; not a distractor-similarity manipulation.
agent_relevance: Irrelevant premises lower accuracy, a loose analogue of distractor load; order randomisation cost reasoning models 5-8 points on several blocks, so order sensitivity persists in 2025 reasoning models.

source: Monk, Meyer, Ngo (2024) Language Models Do Not Possess the Uniquely Human Cognitive Ability of Relational Abstraction (preprint)
finding: Gap 8. Abstract only (full text returned HTTP 403): all tested language models failed the animal-style RMTS test. No accuracy numbers could be retrieved.
numbers: Unknown. The abstract gives no numbers, no model list, no trial counts. Abstract read via Crossref.
limits: Preprint, not peer reviewed; models, prompt format and scoring unverified; contradicted in direction by the 2026 VLM RMTS work (d04) for frontier models.
agent_relevance: Do not cite numbers. Use d04 instead for current model behaviour on RMTS.

source: Penn, Holyoak, Povinelli (2008) Darwin's mistake: Explaining the discontinuity between human and nonhuman minds, Behavioral and Brain Sciences 31(2)
finding: Gap 6. Full text read (70 pages incl. commentaries). The thesis is a symbolic-relational discontinuity. The paper works through domains, not seven numbered claims: similarity (perceptual vs relational), rules, higher-order spatial relations, transitive inference, hierarchy, causal relations, theory of mind, then the relational reinterpretation hypothesis.
numbers: Fagot et al. 2001: baboons fell to chance on different trials when the sample dropped from 16 icons to 2, humans unaffected (entropy account of same/different and RMTS). Baboons needed an average 14,576 extra trials on a conceptual same/different task (Bovet and Vauclair 2001). Only 2 of 7 chimpanzees above chance with identical hiding sites (Kuhlmeier and Boysen 2002). Analogy sensu stricto rests on one chimpanzee, Sarah (Gillan 1981), later shown by Oden et al. 2001 to count featural differences.
quote: there is a significant discontinuity in the degree to which human and nonhuman animals are able to approximate the higher-order, systematic, relational capabilities
limits: Target article with commentaries; 2008 evidence base; the entropy deflation of RMTS was later challenged (Fagot and Maugard 2013).
agent_relevance: The chunking account: success on a relational task can come from a perceptual summary. Check that an LLM solves a relational item by structure, not by a surface statistic.

source: Dymond and Stewart (2016) Relational and Analogical Reasoning in Comparative Cognition, International Journal of Comparative Psychology 29
finding: Gap 10. A methods critique of the hooded-crow RMTS study (Smirnova et al. 2015), plus the Vonk 2015 simple-perceptual-rule account. This is a challenge, not an empirical failed replication.
numbers: No new data. Concerns: nonautomated procedure, correction trials after 2 min with 1-5 min intertrial interval, no observing response, mealworm sounds or smell as cues, no interobserver agreement reported. Each assessment phase: 36 identity trials and 12 RMTS trials over eight sessions; two crows.
limits: Commentary; argues relational matching alone is not analogy because it lacks arbitrarily applicable relational responding.
agent_relevance: Supports caution on the crow claim (K03). Keeps the animal side of the gap contested rather than closed.

source: Musker et al. (2024) LLMs as models for analogical reasoning: order conditions (re-read of design)
finding: Gap 4. In this design permuted-pairs shuffles the order of example mappings inside a question and permuted-questions shuffles question order. The paper does not test averaging over shuffled orders as a fix.
numbers: Human n per condition 14-18 (Defaults 18, Distracted 18, Only RHS 18, Permuted Pairs 17, Permuted Questions 17, Random Finals 15). Earlier recorded: Claude 3 coef -1.78, z=-4.217.
limits: Small human cells; the paper measures sensitivity, not mitigation.
agent_relevance: Averaging or self-consistency over example orders is untested; cost scales with number of orders. Open.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2023) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners (ICLR 2024): search for 2025 follow-ups
finding: Gap 5. A web search and arXiv queries found no 2025-2026 study of self-generated analogical exemplars on reasoning models. Third-party summaries say larger models write better exemplars and that 10 of 50 failures had irrelevant exemplars.
numbers: No new numbers found. Original: GSM8K GPT-3.5 77.8 vs 75.8 CoT (K12).
limits: Absence of evidence from a limited search; summaries are secondary.
agent_relevance: Treat the benefit on strong reasoning models as untested; run it as the agent test.

source: Cross-paper: token cost versus gain (Beger 2025, Camposampiero 2025)
finding: Gap 1. Token costs are barely reported. Only o3 effort (low vs medium, roughly a 16K reasoning budget for medium) and the I-RAVEN-X token ratio (3.4 times) give any number.
numbers: o3 text: low 68.3 to medium 77.1 (+8.8 points). I-RAVEN-X: 3.4 times more tokens and accuracy 86.6 to 17.0. No scaffold-versus-reasoning-model equal-token comparison found.
agent_relevance: No evidence yet that a scaffold beats a reasoning model at equal tokens on relational tasks. A priority measurement for the agent.

source: Beger et al. (2025) repeated-run stability (Appendix J)
finding: Rule choice is unstable across passes even when aggregate accuracy is stable. Single-pass accuracy hides this.
numbers: 48-task subset, 3 runs: same rule class in all passes for 54.2-56.4% of eligible tasks; average pairwise rule-label consistency 66.0-70.9%. Inter-annotator agreement mean 84.8%, kappa 0.70.
limits: Small subset; text medium effort without tools.
agent_relevance: Supports voting over rules rather than answers; indirect evidence for gap 4 (stability cost).
